lines: Telo Ride now installs from Chrome or Edge, and opens in its own window, one tap from the bike.
A web app manifest names it Telo Ride, and opens it at the start, standalone, in the dark ink of the app.
Its icons are the logo mark on ink: one hundred and ninety-two and five hundred and twelve pixels, and a maskable one inside the safe zone.
The spec asks Chromium itself for the manifest it read, and its reasons not to install. There are none. The service worker keeps the icons offline.
Home, where the installed app opens, from a phone to the full screen.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
